inputs.prompt:
Image 1 is a motor-axis layout guide only. Replace dots and lines with a complete industrial product and omit all visible guide marks.
Design a coaxial X8 octocopter for everyday carry-along aerial photography. Strict orthographic top view, nose toward the top edge of the image, arms fully unfolded.
Eight motors in a Coaxial X8 layout: four distinct horizontal axes at the corners of a square. Each of the 4 horizontal axes has two rotors stacked vertically; the lower layer may be occluded in this view. Mean opposite-motor (diagonal) span 250 mm; motor-centre width-to-length span ratio W/L 1.00; adjacent arm angles clockwise from the first motor: 90°, 90°, 90°, 90°.
Match the motor centres and frame links in the attached layout image: dots mark motor centres, lines from the centre mark frame links, and the two crossed straight bars at each dot mark the two stacked propellers at that arm end. Do not reproduce the dots, lines or bars as drawn; render real parts in their place.
Each arm end carries two stationary two-blade propellers stacked on one vertical axis, each 5-inch (127 mm) in diameter. The lower propeller rests at a right angle to the upper one, so from above each arm end shows two straight propellers crossed at their hubs. The two blades of each propeller are identical in length and width and point in exactly opposite directions from the hub, forming one straight blade 180 degrees across, never a V shape.
No propeller guards.
Each arm is 15 mm wide and 4 mm thick; seen from above it reads as a 15 mm wide beam.
Each arm grows out of the shell through a smooth seamless blend, with no joint line at the root.
Fuselage design envelope 150 × 55 × 30 mm (length × width × height); this is a size limit, not a shape.
A rounded pod with a continuous curved outline.
A plain top cover with no seams crossing it.
A forward-facing camera sits at the nose and looks horizontally toward the top edge of the image; no lens glass faces the viewer, and nothing camera-like appears at the tail.
The camera sits inside the nose, flush with the shell; from directly overhead only a thin dark strip of its front window shows at the very front edge of the nose. The camera faces horizontally forward.
No separate landing gear.
Colours by part: body shell silver grey (#c7cbd1); arms silver grey (#c7cbd1); propellers charcoal black (#1e293b).
Shell surface finish: fine matte.
Show the complete product on a plain light background as a photorealistic industrial design rendering. Omit guide marks, dimensions and lettering.
inputs.negative_prompt: flat schematic, line drawing, collage, text, labels, logo, cropped rotor, disconnected arm, extra arm, perspective camera, V-shaped propeller, blades at an acute angle, single-blade propeller, missing blade, unequal blades, camera lens visible from above, upward-facing lens, camera on a neck or stalk, camera on a post
